metadata.title: Odin OS: Cryptographically Authorized Memory Mutation in a RISC-V PMP-Enforced Agent Execution Environment
metadata.description:
Odin OS (Phase B.3.2 Publication Release Candidate) is a bare-metal, zero-allocation (#![no_std]) 64-bit RISC-V microkernel that anchors autonomous AI agent capability boundaries in processor Physical Memory Protection (PMP) comparators. Operating on the central axiom that state which cannot prove its right to exist cannot be committed to memory or disk, Odin OS enforces capability containment via cache-line aligned 256-byte binary tokens termed TransitionDeeds.

This publication release establishes: (1) decoupled Policy Decision Point (PDP) authority isolation supporting both deterministic research fixtures (Mode A) and independently provisioned keys (Mode B); (2) zero-allocation RFC 8032 Ed25519 digital signature verification in pure #![no_std] against a pinned 32-byte root public key; (3) bi-directional W^X memory configuration; (4) dynamic capability lease revocation (SYS_REVOKE_LEASE); (5) a 17-case adversarial matrix under QEMU evaluation; (6) machine-checked formal SMT models via Z3 5.3.1 for bounded integer overflow immunity, memory disjointness, and anti-replay sequence monotonicity; (7) mutation testing sensitivity (15/15 killed); (8) independent Layer B host verification; and (9) end-to-end coupling with local neural inference on google/gemma-4-e4b.
